newsitem.title: JAPAN: Minor quakes continue to hit resort area near Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Minor quakes continue to hit resort area near Tokyo.

text.p: Hundreds of minor earthquakes continued to strike a Japanese resort area south of Tokyo on Tuesday, causing some damage and halting local rail traffic.
There were no reports of injuries, police said.
In the early hours of Tuesday more than 600 tremors, mostly minor ones, shook the Izu Peninsula, a hot spring resort region 135 km (85 miles) southwest of Tokyo, the Meteorological Agency said.
On Monday, the region was shaken by a total of 1,485 tremors, including one measuring 5.2 on the Richter scale.
A landslide triggered by the quakes destroyed a warehouse and a dozen water and gas mains collapsed in the area of Ito on the peninsula's east coast, with a population of 72,000, police said.
Several local residents were evacuated to a nearby city hall, police said.
Local rail authorities said they took precautionary measures to halt rail services to Ito on Tuesday.
Last October, the same region experienced a series of more than 5,000 tremors, only a few of which could be felt without seismic monitoring equipment, the agency said.
